fields.verbatim_quote: On May 3, 2023, the FTC filed a public administrative proceeding seeking substantial changes to the modified consent order, which took effect in April 2020 after its entry by the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia. The changes sought by the FTC are set forth in a proposed order and include, among others, a prohibition on our use of minors' data for any commercial purposes, changes to the composition of our board of directors, and significant limitations on our ability to modify and launch new products.

On May 12, 2023, the IDPC issued a Final Decision concluding that Meta Platforms Ireland's reliance on Standard Contractual Clauses in respect of certain transfers of European Economic Area (EEA) Facebook user data was not in compliance with the GDPR. The IDPC issued an administrative fine of EUR €1.2 billion as well as corrective orders requiring Meta Platforms Ireland to suspend the relevant transfers and to bring its processing operations into compliance with Chapter V GDPR by ceasing the unlawful processing, including storage, of such data in the United States.

In November 2024, the European Commission issued a decision that Meta infringed Article 102 on the Treaty of the Functioning of the European Union in relation to certain alleged business practices relating to Facebook Marketplace and imposed a fine of approximately EUR €798 million.

In March 2024, the European Commission opened an investigation into the compliance of our "subscription for no ads" consent model with requirements under Article 5(2) of the Digital Markets Act. The European Commission issued preliminary findings on July 1, 2024 reflecting its preliminary view that our model does not comply with such requirements, and indicated that it will conclude its investigation by March 2025.

Beginning in January 2022, we became subject to litigation and other proceedings that were filed in various federal and state courts alleging that Facebook and Instagram cause "social media addiction" in users, with most proceedings focused on those under 18 years old, resulting in various mental health and other harms. Putative class actions have been filed in the United States, Brazil, and Canada on behalf of users in those jurisdictions, and numerous school districts, municipalities, and tribal nations have filed public nuisance claims in the United States, Brazil, and/or Canada based on similar allegations.

Through the administrative process, the FTC could amend the order to impose the additional requirements set forth in the proposed order. We should have the opportunity to appeal an FTC decision modifying the order and could request the appellate court to stay the enforcement of the modifications to the order while the appeal is pending. It is unclear whether the appeal or the request for a stay would be successful.

item_7.notes:
[chunk 1/2] This filing section (Item 7 MD&A) is high-level and does not disclose SPVs, VIEs, off-balance-sheet entities, or named investment stakes. The primary SIFI-material signals extracted are: (1) COST_OPACITY from the Jan 2025 useful-life extension of servers/network assets to 5.5 years, reducing 2025 depreciation by ~$2.9B — a classic earnings management lever; (2) CAPEX_ROI_GAP from $39.23B FY2024 capex against a Reality Labs segment burning $17.73B/yr in operating losses with no near-term monetization; (3) EXECUTION_RISK from RL products "only fully realized in the next decade." No Hyperion SPV detail, no specific counterparty capex commitments, and no investment stakes are named in this section — those likely appear in Notes 8/12 (Item 8). Apple and Alphabet are named as counterparties in the ad-targeting risk factor context. The depreciation life change is the highest-confidence hidden signal: extending useful life artificially boosts FY2025 EBITDA without any operational change.
[chunk 2/2] SECTION COVERAGE: This is Meta's Item 7 MD&A section only — it does not contain Notes to Financial Statements (Notes 7, 8, 10, 12, etc. are referenced but not reproduced). Key observations:

1. CAPEX RAMP: Meta guides $60B-$65B capex in 2025, up ~60% from $39.23B in 2024 (including finance lease principal). No specific counterparty named in this section (NVIDIA, custom silicon, etc. would appear in procurement disclosures). Severity 3 — large uncommitted spend with no matched contracted revenue disclosed.

2. FINANCE LEASES: Principal payments on finance leases grew from $850M (2022) → $1.058B (2023) → $1.969B (2024), nearly doubling YoY. These network infrastructure obligations are off-P&L and accelerating — flagged as HIDDEN_LEVERAGE severity 2.

3. REALITY LABS: Cumulative ~$47.5B in operating losses over 3 years with losses still growing. Flagged as EXECUTION_RISK severity 3.

4. OFF-BALANCE-SHEET / SPV: The Hyperion SPV with Blue Owl (reported in other sources) is NOT mentioned in this MD&A section. If it appears in Notes or other sections, it should be extracted from those sections separately.

5. NO INVESTMENT DISCLOSURES in this section — equity stakes in AI labs or compute providers would appear in Note 6 (equity investments) which is not included here.

6. LONG-TERM DEBT: $29.0B senior unsecured notes, maturities 2027-2064, plus $28.1B in future interest obligations. Included in hidden leverage node.

7. UNCERTAIN TAX: $9.99B in unrecognized tax benefits, predominantly transfer pricing and R&D credits — material contingent liability flagged as risk_factor severity 2.

financial_statements_and_notes.notes:
[chunk 1/3] Key findings from Meta's FY2024 10-K financial statements and notes:

1. COST_OPACITY (Severity 3): Meta extended server/network asset useful lives from 4-5 years to 5.5 years effective January 2025. This is a prospective accounting change that will reduce depreciation expense and boost reported operating income without any operational improvement. No dollar-magnitude disclosure of the impact was included in this section.

2. HIDDEN_LEVERAGE (Severity 3): Meta carries $14.9B in operating lease ROU assets and ~$20.2B in total operating lease liabilities (current + non-current) for data centers, offices, and colocations. While the filing states leases generally do not contain material residual value guarantees, the scale of these off-balance-sheet-style obligations is SIFI-material.

3. CAPEX_ROI_GAP (Severity 3): PP&E purchases surged to $37.3B in FY2024 from $27.0B in FY2023, with $7.1B additional sitting in payables as non-cash commitments. Net PP&E stands at $121.3B. No specific contracted revenue is matched against this buildout in this section.

4. COST_OPACITY (Severity 2): $6.07B in non-marketable equity securities in privately-held companies valued using the measurement alternative. Individual investees not named in this section — Note 6 referenced but not provided. Valuation is highly subjective (Level 3).

5. EXECUTION_RISK (Severity 2): Cumulative operating lease impairment charges of ~$5B over FY2022-2024 ($2.22B, $2.43B, $0.38B) suggest persistent overcommitment to physical real estate, raising questions about capital discipline in future facility commitments.

6. OTHER/Tax Risk (Severity 3): IRS transfer pricing dispute with foreign subsidiaries, with IRS stating it will apply position to all subsequent tax years. Long-term income taxes liability has grown to $9.99B from $7.51B.

7. Long-term debt grew to $28.8B from $18.4B, with $10.4B of new issuance in FY2024.

8. China revenue of $18.35B in FY2024 (~11.2% of total revenue $164.5B) represents a geographic concentration risk, particularly given geopolitical tensions.

Note: The Hyperion SPV structure with Blue Owl referenced in the task prompt does not appear in this specific filing section. Note 6 (Non-marketable Equity Securities) was referenced but not provided in the source text — individual investee names are therefore not extractable from this section.
[chunk 2/3] Key SIFI-material findings from Meta's 10-K financial notes:

1. HIDDEN LEVERAGE (Severity 4): $34.12B in uncommenced operating/finance leases for data centers are NOT yet on the balance sheet. This is on top of the $20.23B in present-value operating lease liabilities already recorded plus $709M finance lease liabilities. Total lease exposure including uncommenced is ~$55B+.

2. CAPEX ROI GAP (Severity 3): $32.82B in non-cancelable contractual commitments — critically, $26.34B (80%) is due in 2025 alone. No matched contracted revenue disclosed. Combined with the $34.12B uncommenced leases, total forward infrastructure obligations exceed $66B.

3. EXECUTION RISK (Severity 3): $26.8B construction-in-progress sits on balance sheet but is not yet generating returns. Depreciation on servers/network alone hit $11.34B in 2024, up from $7.32B in 2023.

4. NON-MARKETABLE EQUITY (Note 6): $6.07B portfolio of private company investments. Filing does NOT name individual investees in this section (unlike NVIDIA's Note 8 which enumerates them). No specific AI lab investments named; extraction limited to aggregate.

5. RENEWABLE ENERGY COMMITMENTS: $24.97B estimated spend in multi-year agreements with no fixed/minimum volume — additional contingent obligation not captured in the $32.82B contractual commitments line.

6. LEGAL ACCRUALS OPACITY (Severity 2): $5.52B in legal-related accruals; FTC consent order modification proceedings, GDPR/DSA fines, antitrust trial set April 2025, youth-safety mass arbitration — management acknowledges additional material losses reasonably possible but unquantified.
[chunk 3/3] This filing section (Notes to Financial Statements — Income Taxes, Segment & Geographic Info) contains no off-balance-sheet SPVs, named capex counterparties, or private equity investments. Key extractions:

1. **Tax Contingency / Hidden Leverage**: Meta carries $15.13B gross unrecognized tax benefits (up from $11.67B in 2023), with a net $10.11B potential benefit. Offsetting this, the IRS is asserting up to ~$9.68B in additional federal tax liabilities across two transfer-pricing notices (2010 and 2011–2013 tax years). The Tax Court opinion is expected in 2025, creating near-term resolution risk. Severity 3 (elevated) because the amount is material (~13.6% of 2024 pre-tax income) but Meta has partially reserved per ASC 740.

2. **Reality Labs CAPEX_ROI_GAP**: Three-year cumulative operating losses of ~$47.6B against $6.2B in total RL revenue over the same period. 2024 RL revenue was $2.15B vs. a $17.73B operating loss — a 8.3x loss-to-revenue ratio. This is a sustained structural drag with no disclosed path to profitability, qualifying as a material capex/investment ROI gap.

3. **Cost Opacity — Depreciation DTA**: The deferred tax liability for depreciation/amortization jumped 31.7% YoY to $10.96B, signaling rapid PP&E accumulation consistent with Meta's AI infrastructure buildout. Combined with the $16.74B capitalized R&D deferred tax asset (up from $9.29B), this points to significant balance-sheet inflation from tax-driven capitalization choices that may obscure true economic costs.

No capex commitments with named counterparties, SPVs, VIEs, or private equity investments were disclosed in this specific section.

item_9a.notes: [chunk 1/1] Item 9A (Controls & Procedures) contains no SIFI-material content. The section is pure boilerplate: (1) standard disclosure controls evaluation, (2) management's assessment of internal control over financial reporting per COSO framework, (3) confirmation of no material changes in Q4 2024, and (4) generic limitations language. Item 9B names only routine Rule 10b5-1 trading plan disclosures by board members and officers (Peggy Alford, Christopher K. Cox). Items 10-14 are incorporation-by-reference to the Proxy Statement—no substantive narrative content. No customer concentration, supplier dependencies, investments, related-party arrangements, off-balance-sheet entities, capex commitments, or circular relationships are disclosed in this section. Ernst & Young is named only as the independent auditor of internal controls—a standard audit engagement with no leverage, concentration, or counterparty-risk implications. No extraction warranted beyond confirming Meta's identity."
